title: Event Playbook
description: A data-driven event planning guide that turns answers into dated, assignable tasks, operational advisories and reusable event knowledge.

deadlineCodes.label: Initial planning
deadlineCodes.description: Initial planning milestone, normally around 60 days before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Detailed planning
deadlineCodes.description: Detailed planning milestone, normally around 20 days before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Final arrangements
deadlineCodes.description: Final arrangements milestone, normally around one week before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Commitment decision
deadlineCodes.description: The go-ahead required before additional staffing, purchasing, suppliers or outward communications are firmly committed.

deadlineCodes.label: Final checks
deadlineCodes.description: Final checks milestone, normally the day before the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Final go/no-go
deadlineCodes.description: The final operational confirmation that the event is proceeding, with one decision owner and one communications route.

deadlineCodes.label: Change response
deadlineCodes.description: Immediate coordinated action when an event is cancelled or postponed.

deadlineCodes.label: Immediate follow-up
deadlineCodes.description: Immediate close-down and follow-up work, normally the day after the event.

deadlineCodes.label: Post-event review
deadlineCodes.description: Post-event review and retrospective, normally one week after the event.

modules.title: Start here
modules.description: Define the event and decide which specialist planning modules are required.

items.label: What is the provisional event date?
Does it involve golf?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event involves golf
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Golf team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will any clubhouse room or reserved seating area be used?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether a clubhouse room or reserved seating area will be used
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Clubhouse team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will the event include music, a DJ, live entertainment, a guest speaker or another programmed social activity?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event will include entertainment, music or a guest speaker
dontKnowTask.detail: Agree the intended atmosphere and programme with the organiser, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will food or drink need to be planned specifically for the event?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide if food or drink needs to be planned specifically for the event
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Food & Beverage team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will attendees be charged specifically for entry to the event?
items.helpText: This is separate from ordinary bar purchases, optional food purchases or routine golf fees.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether admission will be charged and agree the pricing principle
dontKnowTask.detail: Confirm whether the event must cover costs, break even or make a contribution, then agree whether an admission charge is needed before publicity begins.

items.label: Will the event need member or visitor communications, advertising or booking information?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether member or visitor communications, advertising or booking information will be needed
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and Communications team, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will there be prizes, presentations, speeches or a formal welcome?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether prizes, presentations, speeches or a formal welcome will be included
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and relevant club teams, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Will staff, volunteers or organisers need specific event-day duties?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether staff, volunteers or organisers need specific event-day duties
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and department leads, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.label: Does the event need a specific safety, safeguarding or contingency review?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event needs a specific safety, safeguarding or contingency review
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the event organiser and responsible club leads, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

modules.title: Event viability and change control
modules.description: Set the decision authority, agree when commitments can be made and coordinate any cancellation or postponement through one source of truth.

items.label: Who has authority to make the final go/no-go decision?
items.helpText: Name one person. Department leads should not have to infer whether the event is proceeding from separate conversations.

items.label: Who owns the single authoritative message if the event changes?
items.helpText: This person coordinates the wording and audience so operational and member messages do not conflict.

items.label: What could cause the event to be cancelled, postponed or placed at risk?
What is the minimum viable attendance, if there is one?
items.helpText: Leave blank where attendance does not affect whether the event proceeds.

items.label: Which teams or commitments must be checked before the event status changes?

options.label: Ticket sales, admission payments or refunds

items.label: Will extra staffing, purchasing or supplier commitments be made specifically for this event?

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether the event requires extra staffing, purchasing or supplier commitments
dontKnowTask.detail: Consult the affected department leads and record what will become difficult or costly to reverse.

items.label: Have members or participants already been told that this event is proceeding?

dontKnowTask.title: Check whether any event communications have already been sent or scheduled
dontKnowTask.detail: Check member email, organiser messages, clubhouse screens, booking confirmations and social channels.

items.title: Agree the event viability criteria, final decision owner and change communication route
items.detail: Record what could stop the event, who decides and who issues the authoritative update to teams and members.

items.title: Confirm the event is proceeding before additional staffing, purchasing, suppliers or publicity are firmly committed
items.detail: The decision owner should mark the event Confirmed or At risk and tell affected department leads before irreversible commitments are made.

items.title: Give Food & Beverage an explicit event go-ahead before arranging extra cover, ordering stock or messaging members
items.detail: F&B should work from the current Playbook status rather than a separate organiser conversation.

items.title: Confirm the event status and agreed wording before sending or scheduling member promotion
items.detail: All departments and the organiser should use the same approved event status and communications owner.

items.title: Record the final go/no-go decision and confirm it with every operational lead
items.detail: Do not rely on silence as confirmation. Mark the event Confirmed, At risk, Postponed or Cancelled in the Playbook.

items.title: Resolve the at-risk event decision and issue one status update
items.detail: Review the recorded risk with the decision owner and either confirm, postpone or cancel the event.

items.title: Coordinate the cancellation or postponement and confirm every interested party has been told
items.detail: The event organiser owns this action. Use the recorded status, reason and agreed wording as the single source of truth, then confirm receipt with everyone already briefed or committed.

items.title: Review and, where possible, cancel additional Food & Beverage cover, extended hours and event-specific preparation
items.detail: This task appears because the plan records F&B work or a briefing. Confirm what was actually arranged, what can be cancelled, reused or returned, and any unavoidable cost.

items.title: Review and release or revise clubhouse rooms, service arrangements and event setup
items.detail: This task appears because completed work, notes or a sent briefing indicate that clubhouse arrangements may already exist.

items.title: Review and release or revise tee times, competition arrangements and course preparation
items.detail: This task appears because a tee-time reservation, completed work, notes or a sent briefing indicates that golf or course arrangements may already exist.

items.title: Stop or replace scheduled event publicity, clubhouse screen artwork and outstanding messages
items.detail: Check the member email schedule, clubhouse screens, booking confirmations and any organiser-managed channels.

items.title: Cancel, postpone or rebook the entertainer or speaker and confirm the financial impact
items.detail: Use the recorded supplier terms, notify the provider through one named contact, release any hired equipment or access arrangements, and record deposits, cancellation fees or replacement-date commitments in Event Finances.

items.title: Stop ticket sales and prevent further admission payments for the changed event
items.detail: Close or amend every sales route, preserve the purchaser and payment records, and make sure public booking links show the same cancellation or postponement status.

items.title: Identify everyone who paid and complete the agreed refunds or ticket transfers
items.detail: Reconcile all payment routes against the purchaser list, apply the published policy consistently, tell purchasers what will happen and record refunds, retained fees or transferred income in Event Finances.

items.title: Issue one authoritative cancellation or postponement update to members and participants
items.detail: Use the wording recorded with the event status. It should replace, not compete with, earlier operational or organiser messages.

items.title: Agree a replacement date or close the postponed event
items.detail: When a new date is known, update the event date and milestones, then return the status to Provisional or Confirmed.

items.title: Record the operational, financial and communication impact of the late change
items.detail: Capture avoidable cost, member confusion and any process change for the next event.

modules.title: Golf
modules.description: Tee-time planning, competition setup, course preparation, registration and golf-day operations.

items.label: Are the required tee times already reserved?
items.helpText: The event date is already fixed. This confirms whether the course allocation for that date has actually been secured.

items.label: Who should arrange the tee-time reservation?

items.title: Agree and reserve the required tee-time allocation with H&C
items.detail: If H&C cannot accommodate the required allocation, return to the event details and reconsider the event date before the rest of the plan is progressed.

items.title: Ask the Professional Shop to reserve the required tee times
items.detail: Confirm the first and last tee-time allocation and any restrictions that apply.

items.title: Arrange the required tee-time allocation for the event
items.detail: The event or section organiser is responsible for securing the tee-time allocation and confirming it in the plan.

items.label: What type of golf is involved?
How many holes will competitors play?
How many holes will actually be played?
items.helpText: Use this for unusual events such as the seven-hole Steeple Chase.

items.label: How many players are taking part?
items.helpText: Include every competitor expected to return to the clubhouse after play.

items.label: How many parents, guardians or other supporters should we plan for around the finish?
items.helpText: Enter 0 if no supporters are expected. This is combined with the player count to estimate clubhouse demand.

items.label: How long do you expect one group to take to complete the round?
items.helpText: Use the likely pace for this age group, competition format and number of holes. This duration drives the expected clubhouse return time.

items.label: How will players start?
What is the first and last tee time?
items.helpText: These times are used to estimate when the first and last groups will return to the clubhouse.

items.label: What time is the shotgun start?
items.helpText: A shotgun start creates a much more concentrated return to the clubhouse because most players finish at around the same time.

items.title: Expected clubhouse return
items.body: The Playbook combines the expected round duration, start pattern, player count and supporter count to forecast the return time and likely operational impact.

items.label: What competition format will be used?
Describe the competition format

items.title: Confirm the competition format, tees, handicap rules and scoring arrangements

items.label: Will results need to be calculated, published or announced on the day?

items.title: Assign responsibility for collecting scores, calculating results and producing the final result

items.label: Are any additional golf fees or payments due on the day?
items.helpText: For example entry fees, sweep payments, visitor green fees or other event-specific charges.

items.label: What needs to be paid, collected or reconciled?

items.title: Confirm how event-day golf fees will be collected and reconciled

items.label: Does the course need any non-standard setup, signage, markers, equipment or hole arrangements?
What non-standard course requirements are involved?

options.label: Special hole setup / obstacles / unusual features
Special tees, markers or course markings
Equipment or consumables to purchase (for example glow sticks)

items.label: Describe the non-standard course setup
items.helpText: Record enough detail that the course team and event organiser know exactly what has to be installed, moved, purchased, printed or removed.

items.title: Agree and document the complete non-standard course setup
Prepare and position all required on-course signage
Prepare and position the selected competition markers
items.detail: Confirm the relevant holes and position the nearest-to-the-pin and/or longest-drive markers before play.

items.title: Print, prepare or obtain the event-specific scorecards or route cards
items.detail: Confirm whether the cards need to be produced internally or obtained from an external competition provider such as the Golf Foundation, then have the correct quantity ready before play.

items.title: Purchase or source all non-standard course equipment and consumables
items.detail: Examples include glow sticks, temporary markers, novelty obstacles, lighting equipment or event-specific materials.

items.title: Brief the Greens Team and schedule installation of special hole features

items.label: Where will players check in or sign in on arrival?

items.title: Prepare and staff the player registration / sign-in point

items.label: Is arrival signage needed outside or inside the clubhouse to direct players to registration?

items.title: Prepare and position arrival and registration signage

items.label: Is a starter or first-tee marshal required?

items.title: Assign a starter or first-tee marshal and provide the event briefing

items.label: Are on-course marshals required?
items.helpText: Consider pace of play, unusual routes, safety pinch points, junior supervision and special-format events.

items.title: Recruit, position and brief the required on-course marshals

modules.title: Presentation and prizes
modules.description: Trophies, prizes, presentation equipment, prize-table setup and the formal running order.

items.label: Are prizes, trophies, vouchers or awards required?
What needs to be presented?
What prizes are required, including the winner categories, quantities and values?
items.helpText: Record enough detail to obtain the correct prizes and approve the overall cost, for example winner, runner-up, nearest the pin, quantity and value.

items.title: Agree the exact prize categories, quantities, values and overall budget
items.detail: Confirm the prize specification with the organiser before anything is ordered, purchased or allocated from existing stock.

items.label: Does a trophy need to be retrieved from the trophy cabinet?

items.title: Retrieve the correct trophy, check its condition and have it ready for presentation

items.label: If it is not in the trophy cabinet, how will the trophy or cup be obtained?

options.label: Collect an existing trophy held elsewhere
Order a new trophy through the Professional Shop
Purchase a new trophy externally through Finance / Accounts

items.title: Collect the existing trophy from its current holder and check its condition
items.detail: Confirm who holds it, when it will be returned and whether cleaning, repair or engraving is required before presentation.

items.label: Who will provide the physical prizes, merchandise, medals or awards?
items.helpText: The Professional Shop is normally the first option, but prizes can instead be bought externally or allocated from items already held.

options.label: Already held by the club or organiser

items.title: Confirm the prizes already held are suitable, complete and reserved for the event
items.detail: Check quantities, condition and location so replacements can still be obtained if anything is missing.

items.title: Order the agreed prizes, trophies, medals or vouchers through the Professional Shop
items.detail: Give the Professional Shop the approved specification and confirm availability, cost, delivery or collection date and how the club will be charged.

items.title: Approve and arrange payment for prizes or vouchers ordered through the Professional Shop
items.detail: Confirm the approved amount, payment method and the invoice or internal charge needed for reconciliation.

items.title: Purchase the agreed external prizes, trophies or vouchers
items.detail: Confirm the supplier, face value or specification, total cost, delivery date and evidence required for payment reconciliation.

items.title: Authorise, prepare and account for the cash or monetary prizes
items.detail: Confirm each amount, how it will be issued, who will hold it before presentation and how receipt or collection will be recorded.

items.title: Agree how the other prizes or awards will be sourced and paid for
items.detail: Record the owner, supplier or holder, approved cost and the date by which each item must be available.

items.label: Do prizes or trophies need winner labels, place cards or presentation notes?

items.title: Prepare winner labels, place cards and presentation notes for the prizes

items.label: Does a prize / trophy table need to be set up?

items.title: Prepare the prize table, presentation cloth and prize display
items.detail: Check that the presentation table, club cloth/tablecloth, trophies, prizes and winner labels are laid out before the presentation starts.

items.label: Will a microphone or PA system be needed for the presentation or announcements?

items.title: Set up and test the microphone / PA system before the presentation

items.label: Does someone need to welcome guests, make announcements or present prizes?

items.title: Assign the presenter and prepare the running order, winners and key announcements

items.label: Should photographs be taken of winners, trophies or the presentation?

items.title: Assign someone to take the required presentation photographs and confirm the shots needed

modules.title: Entertainment and event production
modules.description: Shape the social programme, decide who will deliver it, arrange performers or speakers, and coordinate payment, room and technical requirements.

items.label: What entertainment or programmed social activity is being considered?

options.label: Background music or a club playlist

items.label: What experience are we trying to create, and what should actually happen?
items.helpText: Describe the audience, atmosphere, programme, approximate timings and any important content or restrictions.

items.label: Who will provide the entertainment?

options.label: An external entertainer, speaker or supplier
A mixture of internal and external people

items.title: Agree the entertainment brief, audience, running times and working budget
items.detail: Turn the initial idea into a clear programme that can be quoted, booked, staffed, promoted and delivered.

items.title: Decide whether the entertainment will be delivered internally or by an external provider
items.detail: Compare the available people, quality, cost, equipment and operational risk before committing to the delivery route.

items.label: How will the music be provided?

options.label: A club-managed playlist using house equipment
A live singer, musician or band
Music supplied by another entertainer or organiser

items.title: Prepare, approve and test the event playlist on the clubhouse sound system
items.detail: Confirm who controls the music, the required content and timings, volume limits, playback device, internet dependency and a backup option.

items.label: How will the guest speaker be arranged?

options.label: A club member, officer or staff speaker
An invited external speaker with no fee

items.title: Confirm the speaker, subject, duration, introduction and content boundaries
items.detail: Agree the audience, tone, start time, speaking duration, questions, host introduction and any material or accessibility requirements.

items.label: Which entertainer, speaker or supplier is preferred, and who is the contact?
What will the external entertainment cost, including travel, equipment, accommodation or other expenses?
How will the external entertainer or speaker be paid?

options.label: Card or bank payment in advance

items.title: Book the external entertainer or speaker and record the complete agreement
items.detail: Confirm the date, performance and setup times, fee, deposit, cancellation terms, technical rider, insurance where relevant, contact details and what each party supplies.

items.title: Authorise the entertainment cost and arrange the agreed deposit or payment
items.detail: Give Accounts the supplier, agreed amount, due date, payment method and evidence needed for the event P&L and final reconciliation.

sections.title: Room, technical setup and event-day delivery

items.label: What room or performance-space arrangements are required?

options.label: Audience seating facing the performer or speaker
Lectern, top table or presentation position
Supplier vehicle, loading or early access
No change from the standard room setup

items.label: What technical equipment or services are required?

options.label: Dedicated power, cables or safe cable routing

items.label: Who will be the entertainer or speaker's named club contact on the day?

items.title: Add the entertainment, introductions, breaks and finish time to the event running order
items.detail: Make the hand-offs between food service, announcements, entertainment and close-down explicit, and brief everyone affected.

items.title: Agree and prepare the room layout, performer access and technical setup
items.detail: Translate the entertainment brief and supplier rider into a timed setup plan, including furniture, stage, dance floor, power, cable safety and access.

items.title: Complete the soundcheck and technical test before guests need the room
items.detail: Test every microphone, playback source, presentation, light and connection with the person who will use it, and keep a workable fallback.

items.title: Receive the entertainer or speaker and manage the agreed event-day programme
items.detail: Confirm arrival, access, setup, hospitality, introductions, cues, payment hand-off where applicable and the agreed finish time.

modules.title: Clubhouse
modules.description: Seating, room dressing, audio-visual equipment and digital signage.

items.label: Will there be seated dining or reserved tables for guests?

items.title: Ensure tablecloths and decorations are available
Prepare a seating chart and assign table numbers if necessary
Set up tables and seating according to the agreed arrangement
Remove and store the tables and seating

items.label: Is there a specific theme that the room should be dressed for?
items.helpText: The original playbook notes that some events will not normally require the room to be decorated.

items.label: Do we need to coordinate the decorations with an external party, such as client-provided decorations or an external vendor?

items.title: Confirm theme and decoration requirements with the client or organiser

items.label: Are there any items that need to be ordered to complete the decorations?

items.title: Order supplies to dress the room
items.detail: Create as many individual tasks as are useful if several separate items must be ordered.

items.title: Set up decorations according to the agreed theme
Update the staff briefing in relation to decorating the room

items.label: Do the decorations need to be removed after the event?

items.title: Remove decorations and return the room to its standard setup

items.label: Will a specific channel, such as a sports event, need to be displayed on the screens?
items.helpText: The original playbook notes that this will not normally be required.

items.title: Set up and display the specified channel during the event and record the channel in the plan

items.label: Will digital signage screens display specific images or information?
items.helpText: The original playbook notes that some events will not normally require digital signage screens.

items.title: Prepare artwork and set it up on YoDeck to activate on the event date

modules.title: Catering
modules.description: Food preparation, menus, ordering, vouchers and payment arrangements.

items.label: From what time is catering likely to be required?
Will catering opening hours need to be extended beyond the normal 09:00–17:00 service for this event?
Until what time should catering remain available?
What food service should be available during the extended period?
Will additional catering or bar staffing be needed for the expected post-golf demand?
items.helpText: The return forecast from the Golf module is shown here so that this decision is based on when players are actually expected back in the clubhouse.

items.title: Plan additional catering / bar cover for the expected post-golf demand peak
Agree extended catering hours and service with the Food & Beverage Manager
Confirm staffing cover for the extended catering period
Include the agreed extended catering hours and service in the event-day staff briefing

items.label: Will food be prepared for the event?
Will an external supplier be responsible for providing the food, such as a hog roast?

items.title: Confirm the supplier booking and exchange details of the event
Arrange access to the club and facilities, including power and waste disposal
Include information about the supplier in the staff briefing

items.label: Will we need additional staff to assist with food preparation or serving?

items.title: Coordinate roles and shifts for additional food preparation or serving staff
items.detail: Confirm schedules, specific roles and any required training or briefing for additional helpers working in the kitchen.

items.label: Will the food served be different from the standard club menu?

items.title: Decide what food will be served and agree it with stakeholders
items.detail: Consider seasonal items, event type, guest preferences, budget and dietary restrictions.

items.label: Are printed menus required?

items.title: Create the printed menu design
Arrange for the menu to be printed

items.label: Are menus to be advertised digitally?

items.title: Design the digital menu and set it up to display at the correct time
Include information about the menu in the staff briefing

items.label: When will orders be taken?
Where will orders be taken?

items.title: Set up an order collection method with the Pro Shop staff
items.detail: Ensure Pro Shop staff know the cut-off time for collecting orders, especially where the kitchen is working to a tight schedule.

items.title: Arrange a system for transferring orders to the kitchen
Set up an order collection method with the event organiser
items.detail: Agree whether individual meal choices need to be linked to named people or whether only the total quantity of each meal is required.

items.title: Set up an order collection method for the bar staff

items.label: Should vouchers be issued to be used in exchange for food or drink?

items.title: Design and print a sufficient number of food vouchers, including spares

items.label: Where will the vouchers be issued?
Will there be a charge for the meal?

items.title: Distribute vouchers and advise guests regarding the payment method
Collect all meal payments and provide them to the accounts team

modules.title: Admission, tickets and event payments
modules.description: Agree what people will be charged, how places are sold or reserved, how door payments work and how income is reconciled.

items.label: What will each type of attendee be charged, and what is included in that price?
items.helpText: Record member, visitor, adult or child prices where they differ, and be explicit about whether food, entertainment or other benefits are included.

items.label: What is the maximum number of paid places available?
Will tickets, named bookings or another proof of purchase be required?
How will tickets or paid places be sold and recorded?
When should ticket sales or paid bookings open?
When should advance ticket sales or paid bookings close?
Will anyone receive complimentary or discounted admission?
Who qualifies, who may approve it, and how will it be recorded?

items.title: Approve the admission prices, capacity, inclusions and sales dates
items.detail: Check the proposed income against the event budget and likely attendance before any price or ticket arrangement is advertised.

items.title: Set up and test the agreed ticket or paid-booking route
items.detail: Create the agreed ticket or booking record, apply capacity and sales dates, test the purchase route and give the working link or instructions to Communications.

items.label: Where must the admission price and purchase or booking instructions appear?
What cancellation or refund position should purchasers be told?

options.label: Full refund if the club cancels
Transfer to a new date or refund

items.title: Put the approved admission price, inclusions and purchase instructions into every selected communication
items.detail: Use one approved statement across posters, clubhouse screens, member email, diary and booking confirmations so members see the same price and conditions everywhere.

items.title: Agree and publish the ticket cancellation, transfer and refund terms
items.detail: Resolve the policy before taking money and make the purchaser-facing wording clear enough to use if the event changes.

items.label: When can attendees pay the admission charge?

options.label: Charged to a member or customer account

items.label: Which payment methods will be accepted?
How will door sales, ticket checks, the guest list and walk-ins be handled?
Is a cash float or secure cash handover required for door payments?

items.title: Prepare the admission desk, ticket or guest list checks and facilities for taking door payments
items.detail: Assign named people, provide the final attendee list, define how walk-ins and complimentary places are approved, and test any card terminal before doors open.

items.title: Prepare, record and securely hand over the admission cash float
items.detail: Record the opening float, who receives it, how cash is kept secure and who counts and returns it after admissions close.

items.title: Reconcile tickets, door takings, refunds and complimentary entries against attendance
items.detail: Record the final ticket income in Event Finances, explain differences between tickets and attendance, and provide cash, card and online totals to Accounts.

modules.title: Communications and bookings
modules.description: Promotion, entry information, booking deadlines and participant instructions.

items.label: Who needs to hear about the event?
Do attendees need to book, enter, buy a ticket or confirm attendance?

items.title: Confirm the booking method, capacity, price and closing date

items.label: Should the event be promoted through club channels?

items.title: Prepare and schedule the event announcement across the agreed club channels

items.label: Do attendees need final instructions before the event?

items.title: Send final attendee instructions covering timings, arrival, dress, payment and any event-specific information

modules.title: Staffing and responsibilities
modules.description: Make event-day ownership explicit so important jobs do not remain assumed or unassigned.

items.label: Has one person been identified as the event lead on the day?

items.title: Assign the event-day lead and make their authority and responsibilities clear

items.label: Are there specific arrival, setup, registration, service, presentation or close-down jobs that must be allocated?

items.title: Create the event-day duty list and assign every named job to an individual

items.label: Is a formal staff or volunteer briefing required?

items.title: Prepare and issue the final event briefing with timings, roles, contacts and contingency arrangements

modules.title: Safety and contingency
modules.description: Event-specific safety, safeguarding, first-aid and fallback planning.

items.label: Does the event introduce risks that require a specific risk assessment or control plan?

items.title: Complete the event risk assessment and record any required controls

items.label: Will children or junior members take part in the event?

items.title: Confirm the safeguarding arrangements, supervision and responsible contacts for juniors

items.label: Could weather materially affect the event or require a fallback plan?

items.title: Agree the weather contingency, cancellation decision process and communication route

modules.title: Close-down and follow-up
modules.description: Return the club to normal, settle outstanding items and capture lessons for next time.

items.label: Will anything need to be reset, removed, returned or cleared after the event?

items.title: Assign the event close-down and confirm the clubhouse, course and equipment are returned to their normal state

items.label: Will anonymous attendee feedback be collected for this event?
items.helpText: The retrospective can create a reusable public link and QR code without asking attendees for names or contact details.

dontKnowTask.title: Decide whether anonymous attendee feedback will be collected for this event
dontKnowTask.detail: Confirm the intended audience and how the link or QR code could be distributed, then return to this question and replace Don't know with Yes or No.

items.title: Agree the attendee feedback questions and prepare the event feedback link and QR code
items.detail: Open the event retrospective to create the anonymous form and check its closing date before it is shared.

items.title: Share the attendee feedback form and display its QR code where guests can use it
items.detail: Use the public link in follow-up communications, on event material or via a future membership or ticketing integration.

items.title: Review anonymous attendee feedback and approve the learning to carry into the next event
items.detail: Turn useful evidence into concise organiser-approved notes and map each one to the relevant planner section, question or task.

items.label: Should the organiser record what worked well and what should change next time?

items.title: Complete a short post-event review and update the playbook where a recurring issue or missing question was identified
Complete the post-event retrospective and record financial and operational lessons

advisoryRules.title: Players may return after catering closes
